newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Marines to join anti-kidnapping force.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Marines to join anti-kidnapping force.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos has approved the deployment of officers from the elite Marines to join a police anti-kidnapping unit in the southern Philippines, the government said on Friday.
There were 13 kidnappings in southern Cotabato city last month, ethnic Chinese community leaders said. The victims included a priest, two children and a Chinese-Filipino couple.
The Chinese-Filipino woman was killed by her kidnappers.
Scores of shops in Cotabato shut down their businesses last week in protest against the government's failure to stop the kidnappings.
Nationwide official figures show kidnap gangs abducted a 114 people in the first nine months of this year and collected 36.2 million pesos ($1.35 million) in ransom.
The marines would be the core of the Cotabato unit, the government said in a statement.
Widespread suspicion that kidnap gangs are protected by senior police officers has discouraged victims' families from cooperating with the authorities.
